To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the OntoNL framework can be used to build natural language interfaces for multimedia repositories.
the proposed semantic relatedness measure is a useful tool for natural language interface systems that are built on top of domain-specific ontologies.

(a) the OntoNL framework is a flexible and extensible natural language interface generator; (b) the system is able to handle natural language expressions with rich semantics and disambiguate them in the domain of multimedia; (c) the semantic relatedness measure of ontology concepts can be used for the disambiguation of natural language expressions and the construction of SPARQL queries.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: the design of a natural language system that allows the users to express natural language queries about multimedia resources, the design and implementation a natural language interface generation framework that allows the construction of such natural language systems and a natural language system built using the Ontonl Framework for interactions with multimedia resources.
the development of a system that will allow the users to express their requests in natural language and receive as response a digital object that corresponds to their request.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the OntoNL framework and its applications can be used to generate queries in the SPARQL language from natural language expressions, with a high degree of accuracy.
the OntoNL framework can generate a SPARQL query for a user request, and the system can deliver the digital content that corresponds to the user query.

we have successfully developed an application that is able to understand natural language queries in the domain of multimedia repositories, and generate SPARQL queries that can be executed on the repository.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the system can generate natural language responses for queries that have a rich semantics.

we have developed a natural language system that is able to generate queries for multimedia repositories, and that is based on the use of an ontological knowledge representation of the domain and the application of the semantic relatedness measure of ontologies.
the OntoNL framework can be used to generate natural language queries from natural language expressions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the OntoNL framework can be used to build natural language systems that can interact with knowledge bases and deliver multimedia content.
we can use the OntoNL system to generate queries in SPARQL that can be executed against the multimedia repository and the ontology.
a system for semantic natural language processing and query generation can be constructed with a minimum amount of effort, if the domain of application is already represented by an ontology.
